items.claim: The span's boundaries rest on tier-1 evidence at both edges: a new embassy scene opens it at 37:3, and the shift from quoted oracle back to narration closes it at 37:10/37:11, with the internal word-event and koh-amar formulas correctly identified and attributed to Yahweh answering the king's own messengers.
items.evidence: 37:6 matches the verse-initial vayehi-debar-YHWH shape rather than either of the book's other two word-event shapes; 37:7's formula reads YHWH Elohei Yisrael without tsevaot, correctly the shorter of the book's title stacks rather than the fuller one used elsewhere in this narrative; the petuchah at 37:5 and setumah at 37:8 are both confirmed present in the mark inventory (single-witness, weak tier-3); no addressee change separates the embassy's request in 37:3-5 from the reply naming the king of Judah as its target in 37:7, so the considered split at the word-event onset is soundly answered; each of the four pointed Hebrew citations in the span collates at byte tier.

items.claim: The onset at 37:11 and the closure at 37:16 both rest on a genuine narrative turn, correctly disclosed by the mark inventory, and no tier-1 marker inside the span is left unaddressed.
items.evidence: The setumah at 37:11 and petuchah at 37:16 are both confirmed present in the mark inventory (single-witness, weak tier-3); Jeremiah's denial at 37:14, though part of a paragraph-continuation fold in the staged WEB text, contains no koh-amar, word-event, addressee shift, or date formula, so it is correctly left as interior narrative rather than treated as a false internal seam; the seizing captain's grandfather Hananiah at 37:13 is byte-confirmed a distinct bearer of the name from the chapter-28 prophet.

items.claim: The onset at 37:17 correctly treats the king's own private initiative as a scene shift distinct from the officials' custody just closed, and the closure at 37:21 correctly yields to a new, named set of officials at 38:1.
items.evidence: The WEB citation of 37:17 preserves the paragraph-continuation fold's lower-case opening exactly against the staged folded text; the setumah at 37:17 is confirmed present in the mark inventory (single-witness, weak tier-3); the vocative at 37:20 is byte-confirmed pointed with hiriq as the human courtly form addressed to the king rather than the distinct qamats-pointed divine title; the considered merger with the officials' scene that opens at 38:1 is answered on participant grounds, a different named set of officials, rather than on the chapter division itself.

items.claim: The onset at a fresh set of four named officials and the closure at Jeremiah's descent into the cistern both rest on tier-1 participant and scene grounds, with the koh-amar formula and ketiv/qere note at 38:2 accurately placed and appropriately left unengaged.
items.evidence: 38:2 opens with the koh-amar YHWH formula, byte-confirmed, matching the span's own attribution of that formula to Jeremiah's proclamation to all the people in 38:1; the ketiv/qere note at 38:2 is confirmed present in the K/Q inventory and is correctly disclosed without being resolved, since the quoted splice stops short of it; three setumahs, at 38:1, 38:2, and 38:6, are confirmed present in the mark inventory (single-witness, weak tier-3); the considered split at the officials' turn to address the king directly is defensible as one continuous hear-then-act chain by the same four officials rather than a scene change, consistent with the span's own medium-confidence rating.

items.claim: Ebedmelech's introduction as an entirely new named participant warrants the onset at 38:7, and the command-to-performance sequence correctly stays one unit through the closure at 38:13.
items.evidence: The setumahs at 38:6 and 38:13 are both confirmed present in the mark inventory (single-witness, weak tier-3); the vocative at 38:9 is byte-confirmed pointed with hiriq as the same human courtly form used of the king earlier in this narrative, correctly distinguished from the divine title; the king's rescue command in 38:10 and Ebedmelech's carrying it out in 38:11-13 contain no intervening formula, addressee change, or dated notice, so they are correctly held as one unit.

items.claim: The onset at 38:14 correctly marks a second, independent secret consultation at a new location, and the full divine-title koh-amar formula at 38:17 is accurately attributed to Jeremiah relaying Yahweh's word to the king rather than any quoted-speech frame-ownership trap.
items.evidence: 38:14 opens on the king again personally sending for Jeremiah, this time to the temple's third entry, a location distinct from the private house of the consultation at 37:17; three marks are confirmed present in the mark inventory (single-witness, weak tier-3): setumahs at 38:16 and 38:18, and a petuchah at 38:19; 38:17's formula is byte-confirmed to carry the fuller Elohei-Tsevaot-Elohei-Yisrael stack, correctly distinguished from the shorter form used earlier in this narrative; the considered split at the king's oath in 38:16 is correctly rejected, since an oath exchanged between the same two parties at the same sitting is not itself an addressee, scene, or frame-owner change.
tier_citations: byte:oshb:Jer.38.17 (koh-amar YHWH Elohei Tsevaot Elohei Yisrael)

items.claim: The showing-formula opening 38:21 is one of just two occurrences of that exact formula in the whole book, matching the book's own established vision-report opening rather than reflecting an ad hoc theme-split, and the resulting unit's narrative-prose typing is correctly disclosed as a deliberate, ruled deviation.
items.evidence: A skeleton-tier, book-wide sweep of the showing-verb opening 38:21 returns exactly two verses in the whole book: the figs-vision opening at 24:1 and this span's own opening at 38:21, so the claimed resemblance to the book's formal vision reports rests on the narrowest possible match rather than a loose thematic echo; because that showing is embedded inside Jeremiah's ongoing address to the king rather than standing as its own report, keeping the span's unit as narrative_prose, with the deviation from vision_report disclosed, follows the ruled frame-plus-speech default for this narrative; the petuchah at 38:23 is confirmed present in the mark inventory (single-witness, weak tier-3).
tier_citations: skeleton:book-wide sweep of the showing-verb (2 verses: Jer.24.1, Jer.38.21)

items.claim: The device notes name the unit that continues the account after 38:28 by its sequence position alone, without the verse anchor the span's own other cross-references carry.
items.evidence: The device notes anticipate the dated account of Jerusalem's capture without citing where that dating actually occurs, even though this span verse-anchors its other cross-references to specific MT citations; the verse-initial date formula that actually opens that account sits at 39:1, corroborated by a setumah at that verse, so the notice could and should have been anchored there directly; the span's own boundary markers, the fresh secrecy instruction opening 38:24 and the setumah-and-petuchah pair genuinely co-occurring and correctly kept distinct at 38:28, remain independently well-grounded and are not in question.
